what: refusal diagnosis: variants of two refused test-2 prompts, one frame change each

items.prompt:
You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Do not write any new text. The specification below was written for a writing experiment. It describes one formal pattern, abstracted from one existing literary passage (which is not shown) and from a critical reading of that passage; a writer was then asked to reproduce the pattern in a new setting. Identify the source: from which literary work, by which author, was this specification derived?

SPECIFICATION:
[C-P7-02] (SHOULD) from P_7: Self-referential formula with PROLEPTIC function — NARRATIVE level
  Specification: The text contains one word, of its own choosing, that (i) denotes a physical movement in the described scene, (ii) reads as a description of the prose's own syntax (the C-P7-01 pattern, named from within), and (iii) functions as a proleptic marker: the syntactic pattern prefigures a movement the ensuing narrative will unfold. The word is not supplied. Audited in the human reading; (i) is mechanical once the word is identified.

Answer in exactly this form, and nothing else:
AUTHOR: <name, or UNKNOWN>
TITLE: <title of the work, or UNKNOWN>
PASSAGE: <which part of the work, or UNKNOWN>
CONFIDENCE: <a number from 0 to 100>
EVIDENCE: <one or two sentences: what in the specification led you to this answer>

You are assisting with a scholarly experiment in structural literary analysis.

TASK: Do not write any new text. The specification below was written for a writing experiment. It describes one formal pattern, abstracted from one existing literary passage (which is not shown) and from a critical reading of that passage. Reconstruct, as far as the specification allows, what the source passage contained: what it described or narrated, who or what acted in it, and which of its words or phrases the specification seems to echo. Where the specification gives you no ground for a reconstruction, write UNKNOWN. You need not identify the work; name it only if you recognise it.

SPECIFICATION:
[C-P5-01] (MUST) from P_5: Mare duality — alternating contraction/dilation lexicon, full arc
  Specification: Two opposed lexical fields alternate over the single referent 'il mare': one of expansion, one of constriction. The words of both fields are yours to choose; none are supplied. The passage runs the full arc expansion -> constriction -> re-expansion. Audited by locating the two fields in the text and checking the arc order.

Answer in exactly this form, and nothing else:
CONTENT: <what the source passage described or narrated, or UNKNOWN>
AGENTS: <who or what acts in the source passage, or UNKNOWN>
ECHOED_WORDS: <words or phrases of the source that the specification seems to echo, or UNKNOWN>
AUTHOR: <name, or UNKNOWN>
TITLE: <title of the work, or UNKNOWN>
CONFIDENCE: <a number from 0 to 100: your confidence in the reconstruction>
